chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, both having said:
There is nothing upon the wealth of the orphan regarding the debt and the silent wealth (immovable assets); but as for the produce (crops/gains), upon it is the obligatory charity (Zakat).

key_terms.الْغَلَّات: Produce, gains, or crops generated from wealth
key_terms.الْمَالِ الصَّامِت: Silent wealth (immovable assets or capital that does not generate immediate produce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat on an orphan's wealth?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the principal capital (mal) and its productive yield (ghalawat), establishing that Zakat is levied only on the latter. This ruling ensures that the orphan's wealth is preserved from depletion by taxing only the surplus gains, a principle widely accepted by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi.

en.hubeali: Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, both having said,
‘There is nothing upon the wealth of the orphans regarding the debts and the silent wealth (immovable asset). But, as for the produce, so upon it is the Obligatory charity (Zakāt)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Hammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
Zakat is not due on loans people owe to orphans’ as well as on the orphans immoveable assets; however, it is obligatory to pay Zakat for the orphans’ grains.’”
